newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil closes $1.50 firmer, Brent $17.88.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil closes $1.50 firmer, Brent $17.88.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures closed towards the lower end of the day's range under pressure from weaker Brent and U.S. crudes, brokers said.

Front month July gas oil last traded at $161.75 a tonne, up $1.50 from Wednesday but only $1 off the day's low. The contract opened at $163 and touched a high of $163.25 early on before crude trading began.
"Again it's been a case of the crude dog wagging the gas oil tail," a broker said.
"It fell apart on steady hedge selling. The European trade has been very keen to sell the market."
Gas oil's slide was braked by bedrock support for U.S. heating oil at 52.10 cents a gallon -- a level breached after gas oil closed.
Front month August Brent crude futures were trading down 34 cents at $17.88, four cents off the low, driven down by scepticism over OPEC's ability to stick to renewed pledges of quota adherence.
Brokers said bears had taken heart from an OPEC denial that Venezuela had admitted overproducing at the group's six-monthly talks in Vienna this week.

Brokers said any such admission would have been a constructive sign that members were facing reality and prepared to work to achieve a solution. The denial implied face-saving for quota-busters was more important than price support, they said.
IPE July gas oil was trading $1.50 firmer at $161.75 a tonne, catching up on Brent's late gains yesterday.
Brent made a big 34-cent gain on Wednesday following declarations by OPEC that it would cut back on over-production.
OPEC leaders on Thursday confirmed the previous day's deal to stick to previously agreed production ceilings.
